name: What is the difference between turnover maintenance and occupied rental repair?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between turnover maintenance and occupied rental repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turnover maintenance focuses on bringing a vacant unit back to market-ready condition for a new tenant, whereas occupied maintenance addresses specific, immediate repairs while a resident lives there. Turnovers allow for noisy, multi-room projects like comprehensive interior painting, heavy drywall sanding, tile demo, and subfloor work without disruption. Occupied repairs require careful scheduling, dust containment, and focused scopes—such as fixing a leaking vanity drain or patching a single wall—to respect the tenant’s living space and daily schedule.
acceptedAnswer.description: Turnover maintenance handles full refreshes like repainting and tile work in empty units, while occupied repair targets specific, urgent fixes with minimal tenant disruption.
